meta.title: Devices and acceleration | ProxMenux
meta.description: How OCI manager Apps passes GPU, NVIDIA, Coral, USB, FUSE and other devices to an OCI container as validated native Proxmox VE resources.

header.title: Devices and acceleration
header.description: GPU, NVIDIA, Coral, USB, FUSE and block devices become validated native Proxmox VE resources of the container.

sections.title: The device the application needs, not the whole host

blocks.p: A device requested by the Compose file or by the application profile becomes a concrete devN entry or LXC mount. Asking for a GPU, a USB device or a Coral does not make the container privileged.

calloutWarning.title: Detected devices are not attached on their own
calloutWarning.body: The host is inventoried, but only devices declared by the Compose file or by a compatible profile are offered and attached. A GPU, USB dongle or Coral present on the host is not exposed to every LXC.

sections.title: How the host device is identified
sections.intro: Before the LXC is modified, the device is read on the host and matched against the chosen profile.

items.title: The template offers its profiles
items.body: For example CPU only, Intel/AMD VA-API, AMD OpenCL, Intel OpenCL or NVIDIA. The options belong to the image, not to a common menu.

items.title: A profile is chosen
items.body: It defines the device nodes, environment, mods or runtime the application needs.

items.title: A path is proposed
items.body: For DRM, /dev/dri/renderD128, which can be changed on a host with several render nodes. For USB or serial, the concrete node is selected.

items.title: Validation
items.body: Existence, type, allowed vendor, permissions and GID are checked. A mismatch stops the operation.

items.title: The contract is written
items.body: Path, mode, GID, write access and profile are recorded for updates and recreations.

items.title: Attach and test
items.body: pct set adds the devN entry and access is then checked inside the LXC. LinuxServer images are also checked as user abc.

sections.title: How it appears in the LXC configuration
sections.intro: Illustrative values: dev0 and dev1 are the free slots Proxmox VE assigns, and renderD128, apex_0 and the GID depend on the hardware of the node.

blocks.p: The GID is read with stat on the host and written to the devN entry; the render and video groups are not assumed to have a fixed number. The device keeps the same /dev path inside the LXC, where the application's own mechanisms look for it.

calloutWarning.title: Node requirement: NVIDIA Container Toolkit
calloutWarning.body: A working driver on Proxmox VE is not enough to give an NVIDIA GPU to an OCI image. OCI manager Apps uses nvidia-container-cli, from the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, to identify the devices and to obtain the binaries and libraries that match the loaded driver.

blocks.p: The ProxMenux NVIDIA installer installs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit from the official NVIDIA repository together with the driver. It checks its four packages, validates nvidia-container-cli and records the result in the change journal of Audit & Report.
These two commands on the host show whether the driver and the Toolkit are available:
On a host where the driver was installed by other means, the Toolkit is installed from the official stable repository:

shell.code:
apt-get update
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl gnupg2

curl -fsSL https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/gpgkey \
  | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/nvidia-container-toolkit-keyring.gpg

curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/stable/deb/nvidia-container-toolkit.list \
  | sed 's#deb https://#deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/nvidia-container-toolkit-keyring.gpg] https://#g' \
  > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-container-toolkit.list

apt-get update
apt-get install -y nvidia-container-toolkit libnvidia-container-tools

blocks.p: The inventory OCI manager Apps uses is the output of:

calloutInfo.title: Docker runtime configuration is not involved
calloutInfo.body: The containers are native LXCs and no Docker daemon is used, so nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker plays no part: ProxMenux queries nvidia-container-cli directly and writes the LXC devices and mounts. The commands and supported platforms are maintained in the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installation guide.

items.title: Inventory from the driver
items.body: nvidia-container-cli lists the device nodes, binaries, firmware and libraries of the installed driver.

items.title: No fixed version
items.body: The template does not name library files. The profile is generated from the current host.

items.title: Read-only mounts
items.body: The host libraries are mounted read-only instead of being copied into the container.

items.title: Driver changes
items.body: After a driver change the inventory is generated again before the affected LXCs start.

code.title: NVIDIA result (simplified)
code.code:
devN: path=/dev/nvidia0,...
devN: path=/dev/nvidiactl,...
devN: path=/dev/nvidia-uvm,...
lxc.mount.entry: HOST_LIBRARY CONTAINER_LIBRARY none ro,bind,create=file 0 0

blocks.p: Passing only /dev/nvidia0 is not enough. The user-space components of the loaded driver are mounted read-only, and nvidia-smi then runs inside the LXC to compare GPU, UUID, PCI bus and version with the host inventory.

calloutWarning.title: USB numbering can change
calloutWarning.body: A path such as /dev/bus/usb/003/004 can change when the device is reconnected or the host restarts. The profile records vendor, product and serial when they are available, but a new bus address is not remapped automatically.

blocks.p: A peripheral is given by its concrete node: /dev/ttyUSB0, /dev/ttyACM0, /dev/apex_0 or /dev/bus/usb/BBB/DDD. Passing the whole of /dev is not accepted. Coral is offered only to applications whose profile declares it.

blocks.p: Concrete devices, optional privilege, required privilege, AppArmor or seccomp relaxation and access to the host PID namespace are treated as separate cases, not under one generic privileged label. Each option with a risk is explained and confirmed during the installation.
